reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays but keeps the new isWeekendOrHoliday predicate private, so schedules/app.ts re-implements the non-working-day test inline (without the MM-DD form) in two handlers instead of reusing it.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && daily && (isWeekend || holidays.includes(day))' check is written twice in schedules/app.ts in addition to isWeekendOrHoliday and the getNextDate daily loop, and the skip-or-move per-occurrence block is repeated across getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Moving logic and the holiday predicate sit in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-vs-move dispatch and a second holiday test live in server handlers, and schedule-template keeps its own inline weekend ternaries without the daily rule.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the weekend/holiday paths, the new handler, the RecurConfig type and tests.

maintainability.why: The holiday definition already diverges between the shared predicate (supports MM-DD) and the inline copies in app.ts (full dates only), showing how the scattered rule will drift on every change.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange test d.isWeekend/config.holidays.includes directly instead of using the shared non-working-day predicate; schedule-template.ts decides weekend moving inline.

disguised_duplication.where: isWeekendOrHoliday in shared/schedules.ts is re-expressed as an inline filter predicate in getUpcomingDates and as an if-return-null in getDatesInRange (schedules/app.ts), each slightly different.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a holidays parameter; getNextDate gained a daily skip loop; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template createScheduleList decide the daily/holiday rule themselves.
